q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT DISTINCT(P1.EMAIL) AS EMAIL FROM PERSON P1 INNER JOIN PERSON P2 ON P1.EMAIL = P2.EMAIL AND P1.ID <> P2.ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT(P1.EMAIL) AS EMAIL FROM PERSON P1 INNER JOIN PERSON P2 ON P1.EMAIL = P2.EMAIL AND P1.ID <> P2.ID
explanation: Both queries aim to retrieve distinct email addresses that appear more than once in the PERSON table. Q1 uses GROUP BY with HAVING to filter groups with more than one occurrence. Q2 uses a self-join to find pairs of persons with the same email but different IDs, then applies DISTINCT to get unique emails. They are logically equivalent.
